correctness.rationale: For any \(k\) simplex vertices, the sum vector has squared norm \(k(n-k+1)/n\) and inner product \((n-k+1)/n\) with each selected vertex. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives the exact onset \(\cos\theta\le\sqrt{(n-k+1)/(kn)}\), with equality at the normalized sum. Thus triple overlaps begin at \(\theta_{3,n}\) and positive-measure quadruple overlaps do not begin until \(\theta_{4,n}\), so inclusion--exclusion terminates exactly after the triple term on the claimed interval. Projecting uniform spherical measure to the three-vertex span gives the stated density; inversion of the regular-simplex Gram matrix gives the quadratic form and Jacobian. Scaling about the triple-contact point reduces the onset integral to a three-simplex beta integral and gives power \((n+1)/2\) with the displayed gamma coefficient. The assigned verifier checks the Gram inverse, determinants and beta identity exactly; a separate numerical integral near onset was consistent with the coefficient.
residual_risks: The onset asymptotic is intentionally restricted to dimensions at least five.

originality.rationale: Arman, Kaire and Prymak give exact one-cap and two-cap formulas and then use second-order Bonferroni for simplex-centred caps. Full inspection shows their Lemma 2 states pairwise exactness up to the dimension-independent angle \(\arccos(1/3)\); for dimensions at least four the regular-simplex Gram calculation yields a smaller true triple-overlap onset. The audited theorem therefore not only supplies the missing three-cap integral and onset asymptotic but also corrects the first-overlap regime before extending the exact union formula to the quadruple threshold. Resultary search returned the assigned record as the exact same-object hit and no stronger prior third-order formula.
